title: Narrow sacred-status interpretation to defeasible weight in the asked tradeoff
author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: The rule reports that sacred status can have independent normative weight from RCI012@1 and RCI029@1. The broad phrase can be read as attitude-independent value or strict inviolability, although the some answer permits tradeoffs and neither item tests attitude independence. The sole rule source is context-limited empirical work.
proposedBehavior: Keep exact item revisions, route item assignments, and answer mappings. State only that sacred status itself can carry at least some moral weight in the asked community-object and practical-benefit case. Link philosophical sources to the scoped claim and stronger neighboring theses. Keep missing, lean, mixed, and opposing behavior unchanged. No tradition affinity is added.
rationale: The some response to RCI029 allows benefit to outweigh status. RCI012 asks for a special reason but not an attitude-independent metaphysical property. The symbolic response values human relationships without granting additional weight to status itself. The revised claim tracks these answer meanings and prevents stronger false positives.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: In the stated community-object and practical-benefit case, sacred status itself can carry at least some moral weight beyond the object's ordinary resource value and the specified direct harm to persons.
neighboringViews: Only human reactions and relationships matter in the vignette, with no additional sacred-status weight
Sacred status carries some defeasible moral weight
Sacred values are strictly inviolable and ordinary tradeoffs are forbidden
Sacredness is independent of community attitudes or practices
Sacredness requires a religious or purity-based account
nonEntailments: Sacred and practical values are incommensurable
A deity, revelation, religious law, purity norm, or religious identity
The same judgment applies to persons, places, or political commitments
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: The old label can imply a stronger thesis than RCI012 and RCI029 discriminate. The sole context-limited empirical source does not supply a claim-level philosophical basis or validate the two authored units.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: Katsafanas describes a stronger three-part account of sacred values involving inviolability, incontestability, and dialectical invulnerability. Rotondo discusses ethical significance of sacredness without making this questionnaire a measure of that full theory. Philosophers also dispute the senses of value incommensurability. This release infers none of those broader theses.

sourceClaims.claim: Sacredness can have ethical significance, including for political morality; this supports distinguishing a sacred-status reason from an object's merely practical use without establishing this questionnaire's validity.

One influential account treats sacred values as inviolable, incontestable, and dialectically invulnerable; assigning only some defeasible weight in a tradeoff does not establish those stronger properties.
Philosophers distinguish multiple meanings of value incommensurability and comparability; assigning some moral weight in one case does not settle those separate theses.

alternatives: Keep the broad independent normative weight wording: rejected because it invites intrinsic or attitude-independent readings.
Infer inviolability from the very high answer: rejected because one comparative case does not settle absolute tradeoff constraints.

Add new questions for stronger sacred-values doctrine now: deferred because this release corrects the existing result; a stronger proposition would require its own discriminating items and evidence review.
Treat the two authored units as empirically independent: rejected because no response-process or participant data establish that claim.
respondentImpact: The same raw answers retain their evidence states, but the communicated proposition becomes narrower. Full can still support or oppose the scoped claim; Quick and Standard lack both required units. Historical results keep their original wording; current reinterpretation remains separate.
historicalCompatibility: Preserve model release 1.15.0 and all previous item, rule, route, source, catalog, localization, and engine artifacts. No item wording or raw response is rewritten. The successor uses a new model and manifest, while historical administrations replay their pinned release.

approvals.note: Reviewed the exact item meanings, Rotondo's peer-reviewed abstract, Katsafanas's stronger sacred-values account, SEP value incommensurability, and the community-conferred, secular and tradeoff-permitting neighbors.
Reviewed unchanged item revisions and evidence mappings, successor model and source records, route rebinding, historical replay, result wording and regression cases.

release.migration: No raw-response migration. The new rule narrows interpretation only; all route question revisions and order are retained.
